title: Define Security Requirements for Software Development
gap: Open: PO.1.1, PO.1.3.

title: Security requirements for the development infrastructure and processes
gap: The security rules of the build and CI infrastructure (read-only token, pinned actions, hashed tools) are in the workflows but not written down as requirements.

title: Security requirements for the software itself, kept current
Requirements told to third parties who supply components
gap: No security requirements are sent to the suppliers of models, hardware or services; open-source components are taken as published and gated by the scans.

title: Implement Roles and Responsibilities
Roles and responsibilities across the SDLC
gap: No security owner is named at Aimedics (soa.csv 5.2, REG-031) and no role is written for each security activity of the development life cycle.

title: Role-based secure-development training
gap: No secure-development training exists or is recorded; a builder's training is its card and brief (QMS-lite section 3).

title: Management commitment to secure development
gap: No written commitment of the company's management to secure development exists in the repository.

title: Implement Supporting Toolchains
gap: Open: PO.3.3.

title: Which tools each toolchain must have
Tools and toolchains deployed and kept securely
Tools produce artefacts of their checks
gap: The secret and static security scans leave only a CI log: no SARIF or JSON result is kept per run or per release.

title: Define and Use Criteria for Software Security Checks
gap: Open: PO.4.2.

title: Criteria for security checks, tracked through the SDLC
Information for the criteria gathered and safeguarded
gap: The release gates write a record per build, but the results of each pull request's scans expire with the CI artefacts and there is no one security record per release.

title: Implement and Maintain Secure Environments for Software Development
gap: Open: PO.5.1, PO.5.2.

title: Development environments separated and protected
gap: Building uses synthetic data only and CI runs on fresh hosted runners, but how the development, build and test environments are kept apart and protected is not written down or checked.

title: Development endpoints secured and hardened
gap: Nothing sets or checks the hardening of the machines and agent sessions that develop, build or sign TrialBox.

Create Source Code by Adhering to Secure Coding Practices
gap: Open: PW.5.1.

title: Secure coding practices followed
gap: Ruff's S rules and bandit enforce part of secure coding, but there is no written secure-coding standard and ruff's S rules are off for tools/ and tests/.

title: Configure the Compilation, Interpreter, and Build Processes to Improve Executable Security
gap: Open: PW.6.1, PW.6.2.

title: Compilers, interpreters and build tools with security features
gap: The interpreter and base images are pinned by digest and every install is hash-checked, but no one has decided which interpreter or JVM security features to use.

title: Build tool settings decided, configured and used
gap: Dockerfile settings are checked by hadolint on 3 of the 6 Dockerfiles only.

title: Review and/or Analyze Human-Readable Code to Identify Vulnerabilities and Verify Compliance with Security Requirements
gap: Open: PW.7.2.

title: Decide on code review and code analysis
Code reviewed or analysed; issues recorded and triaged
gap: Bandit runs at medium severity and confidence and honours inline nosec lines outside the reviewed ledger, and no person reviews code before it merges.

title: Test Executable Code to Identify Vulnerabilities and Verify Compliance with Security Requirements
gap: Open: PW.8.2.

title: Decide on executable code testing
Tests scoped, designed, run and documented
gap: There is no dynamic scan of the running console, no fuzzing of the parsers and no penetration test yet.

title: Configure Software to Have Secure Settings by Default
gap: Open: PW.9.2.

title: A secure baseline for every security-relevant setting
Secure defaults implemented and documented for administrators
gap: The containers run without dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges or read-only file systems.

title: Identify and Confirm Vulnerabilities on an Ongoing Basis

title: Code reviewed and tested for undetected vulnerabilities
gap: Reviews sample the code for vulnerabilities from time to time; deeper analysis (own Semgrep rules, a secret scan of the git history) is not run.

title: Vulnerability disclosure and remediation policy
gap: There is no vulnerability disclosure policy and no public security contact.
